clue.text: After pooling the stakes it distributes the winnings of course

definitions.text: After pooling the stakes it distributes the winnings of course

parts.words: After pooling the stakes it distributes the winnings of course
parts.note: describes a betting system at a racecourse where all bets go into one pool and the takings are shared among winners

explanation.surface: Someone explains how prize money is handed out once all the bets are gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means 'at the racecourse': this is the French-named pooled betting system.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool-betting system that divides the total stake among the winning tickets is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Smart fellow?

parts.note: the phrase smart-somebody names a know-all, a cocky clever person

explanation.walkthrough: A know-all is called a 'smart ___', so the fellow is the man's name in that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom for a cocky know-all, this man's name follows 'smart'.

clue.text: Use force to gain entrance

parts.note: describes bursting violently into a place

explanation.surface: Advice to a burglar or a policeman at a locked door.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst in suddenly and violently, as invaders do, is to force one's way inside.

clue.text: Drug one is made to experience

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are made into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A patient is forced to take a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is made to' signals rearranging DRUG ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through or suffer something is a verb synonym.

clue.text: A piece of wilful vanity in the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small display of self-love takes place on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island sits across 'wilfUL VAnity'; the definition is the place, an island off Mull.
explanation.definitionFit: This small island lies off the west coast of Mull, one of the Inner Hebrides group of Scottish isles.

clue.text: Nor 9 disrupted could make a good bit in the past

definitions.text: could make a good bit in the past

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer to 9-across, the old Italian currency units

explanation.surface: A muddled note claiming someone once earned plenty of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' shuffles NOR with LIRE (9-across). 'a good bit' is not money but the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic craftsman who made bits, spurs and metal harness fittings for horses.

clue.text: Drink prescribed by the medical profession?

definitions.text: Drink prescribed by the medical profession?

parts.words: Drink prescribed by the medical profession?
parts.note: doctors prescribe a regime of only fluids, so the drink is the whole menu

explanation.surface: A doctor writes out a prescription for something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime of fluids only, ordered by doctors, is nourishment taken as drink.

clue.text: Obstinately self-willed principal with powerful following

indicators.note: the second word comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a principal of a school is its head
powerful means strong

explanation.surface: A stubborn headteacher backed by a mighty group of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly insisting on one's own way is a synonym phrase for wilful.

clue.text: Fifty-one Engineers required to meet expenses in Italy.

definitions.text: required to meet expenses in Italy

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Fifty-one army engineers are needed to cover costs in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty-one' is not a number but two Roman numerals, L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the currency units of Italy before the euro, so they paid costs there.

clue.text: A seaman who gets completely immersed in the pursuit of wealth

definitions.text: A seaman who gets completely immersed in the pursuit of wealth

parts.words: A seaman who gets completely immersed in the pursuit of wealth
parts.note: reads like a greedy man, but literally describes someone who goes underwater to collect gems from oysters

explanation.surface: A sailor wholly absorbed in getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who swims to the seabed to gather oyster gems is literally submerged seeking riches.

clue.text: Gets brought into action and given out?

parts.note: gets as in 'gets fined' means is
brought into a legal action, taken to court, means sued

explanation.surface: Someone is called up for duty and handed equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Distributed or released officially, as supplies or stamps are.

clue.text: The loss incurred when we hedge a speculator on the Stock Exchange

indicators.note: to hedge is to surround, so the first word is placed around the following ones

parts.note: a stag buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit

explanation.surface: A finance tale about losses made while hedging a market gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedge' sounds like a finance term but here means 'enclose', and the stag is a share-dealer, not a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste or the amount squandered is the money or material lost.

clue.text: The liquid notes of Handel?

parts.note: liquid notes reads as flowing melody, but names Handel's suite written for a river party on the Thames

explanation.surface: Praise for the flowing melodies of a great composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel composed this orchestral suite for King George I's barge trip on the Thames.

clue.text: What one needs to equip oneself as a handyman

definitions.text: What one needs to equip oneself as a handyman

parts.words: What one needs to equip oneself as a handyman
parts.note: describes the kit of hammers and spanners a handyman carries

explanation.surface: Advice for someone setting up as an odd-job man.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete kit of implements for repairs is a handyman's equipment.

clue.text: Sheer agony for Sandown Park?

indicators.note: agony suggests writhing, so the letters of the word before twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A punter suffers terribly at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agony' signals rearranging SHEER. Sandown Park is a racecourse in Surrey; the question mark says it is one example of what is in the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town where Sandown Park racecourse is located, so the park stands for its home town.

clue.text: Injured pride associated with Old Testament precious stone

indicators.note: injured suggests damage, so the letters of the word after are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's hurt pride is tied to a jewel from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A green gemstone, a gem-quality form of olivine.

clue.text: Type of nut a chartered accountant has to write about

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for write goes round the other

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: An accountant must write about some kind of eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' tempts as a madman; it is the tree fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-shelled nut from a hickory tree of the southern United States.

clue.text: A tree I get sore about when rattled

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters of the words before get jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross about a tree when flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rattled' shakes up I and SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Carry a gun, perhaps, that's a shorter version of!

explanation.surface: Someone explains that to carry a firearm is a brief way of saying it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the short name of the totalisator, the racecourse pool betting machine; the clue seems to point back at 1-across, whose number may be lost from the printed text.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry, especially a gun, is American slang; and it is also the clipped form of totalisator, the betting machine.

clue.text: I'd look around for a place in which to bathe

definitions.text: a place in which to bathe

indicators.note: around means the word for look goes round the other piece

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they would search around for a spot to swim.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the old word 'behold', a crossword staple for 'look'.
explanation.definitionFit: A public open-air swimming pool or beach resort is a spot for swimming.

clue.text: Highland plane redirected

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are sent in a new direction, rearranged

explanation.surface: A flight is diverted over mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highland' tempts as Scotland, but means a mountainous country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom is literally a high country, home to Everest.

clue.text: Toggle for a belt of Japanese design

definitions.text: Toggle for a belt of Japanese design

parts.words: Toggle for a belt of Japanese design
parts.note: describes the small carved fastener used to hang a pouch from a kimono sash

explanation.surface: A belt fastener in a Japanese style.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved toggle of ivory or wood holding items hung from a kimono sash.

clue.text: Any fat about to put a knife or a whistle on?

definitions.text: to put a knife or a whistle on?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for fat goes round the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A question of whether fat can be spread on cutlery or a whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a strange question about spreading fat; it means a cord to hang things on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord worn round the neck or shoulder for holding a whistle or knife, as sailors do.

clue.text: His business is to clarify the matter

definitions.text: His business is to clarify the matter

parts.words: His business is to clarify the matter
parts.note: reads as someone explaining an issue, but describes a man who purifies sugar or oil

explanation.surface: A man whose job is to explain the issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clarify' means purify and 'matter' is material, not an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who purifies raw substances such as sugar, oil or metal removes impurities from material.

clue.text: A purely nominal attach ment?

parts.note: nominal attachment reads as a token affection, but is literally something attached that shows a name

explanation.surface: A relationship that exists in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge pinned or tied on to show who someone is, so it is attached and bears a name.

clue.text: What a company must do to get dollars out of wine?

definitions.text: What a company must do to get dollars

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A firm earning foreign currency by selling its wine abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling goods overseas brings foreign currency into a firm.

clue.text: Teutonic sea-wolves that hunted in packs.

definitions.text: Teutonic sea-wolves that hunted in packs.

parts.words: Teutonic sea-wolves that hunted in packs.
parts.note: describes German submarines that attacked convoys in groups called wolf packs

explanation.surface: German sea predators hunting in groups.
explanation.definitionFit: German submarines of the World Wars operated in coordinated wolf packs against shipping.

clue.text: A stage favourite's comeuppance

indicators.note: read as come up, in a down clue the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A theatre star gets their just deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeuppance' splits as 'come up', reversing PETS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage in a process is one step along the way.

clue.text: A fund only partially open

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A fund that is only partly accessible.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or unwrap something is a verb synonym.

clue.text: To a certain extent how the steeplejack will work?

explanation.surface: A steeplejack does his job only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly; literally a steeplejack works high on a spire's tip.

clue.text: Misfortunes we keep well away from.

definitions.text: Misfortunes we keep well away from.

parts.words: Misfortunes we keep well away from.
parts.note: keep well away reads as avoid, but also means stay healthy and so avoid sicknesses

explanation.surface: Troubles we try to avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles and sicknesses are what a healthy person is free of.

clue.text: The speed required to map out new territory, maybe

definitions.text: required to map out new territory, maybe

explanation.surface: Haste needed to chart unknown lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means promptness, and also a journey of exploration into unknown country.
